note: Synthetic persona library for pressure-testing a Brand Engagement Plan. Each persona is a named, fictional individual that embodies one behaviour-based audience segment (config/audience_segments.json) for a specific specialty/therapy area in the client roster. Demographics, prescribing volumes (TRx = total monthly prescriptions for the therapeutic class, NRx = new starts), digital-affinity scores and channel preferences are illustrative but calibrated to current HCP-engagement research (Indegene HCP Digital Affinity ~84% want to sustain/grow digital; ~68% webinars a primary channel; ~78% prefer a virtual+in-person mix; rep access <35% in the US) and to specialty prescribing patterns (oncology/nephrology lower absolute volumes than primary care/cardiology). They exist so a plan can be reviewed 'in character' by the people it is trying to reach. Not real individuals; any resemblance is coincidental.
disclaimer: Fictional composites for simulation. TRx/NRx and digital scores are directional, not market data.

personas.name: Dr. Elena Rossi
personas.tagline: The efficient digital native who will not take a rep meeting
personas.bio: High-throughput community oncologist who runs an evidence-first practice. Reviews new data herself the week it drops, keeps her own comparison notes, and treats her inbox as her primary channel. Reps almost never get past the front desk; she'd rather have a link than a lunch.

prescribing.brand_stance: open but unconvinced — needs to see head-to-head relevance to her patient mix

tolerated: Occasional live virtual detail if it's short and data-led
channels.f2f_stance: Declines almost all in-person meetings; no rep lunches
channels.email_stance: Reads relevant, concise email on her own schedule; deletes generic blasts unopened
channels.best_moment: Early morning before clinic, and Friday admin block

motivations: Getting to the differentiating data fast
Content tailored to her HR+/HER2- patient mix
frustrations: Reps who can't answer a data question
Being re-contacted across five channels with the same message
Fluffy, claims-first messaging with no numbers
decision_drivers: Head-to-head efficacy vs standard of care
personas.tone: Direct, time-pressured, data-driven, a little impatient
personas.voice_sample: Make it quick and make it relevant to my patients, or I'm closing the tab. Don't send a rep — send me the data.
what_earns_engagement: A concise, personalized email with the head-to-head data and a one-click link to the evidence
An on-demand webinar she can watch at 6am
Frequency discipline — one coordinated message, not five

personas.name: Dr. Marcus Bell
personas.tagline: The relationship-led prescriber who decides over a face-to-face conversation
personas.bio: Respected community cardiologist with a loyal referral base. Forms his decisions through trusted rep relationships and peer conversations, not portals. He'll adopt when a rep he trusts walks him through the evidence and a colleague vouches for it.

prescribing.brand_stance: cautiously loyal to what works; will switch on trusted, in-person evidence

tolerated: A short email recap after a rep visit
channels.f2f_stance: Prefers and expects in-person; the relationship is the channel
channels.email_stance: Will read a brief recap tied to a conversation he already had
channels.best_moment: Scheduled lunch details; after-hours peer dinners

motivations: Trusted guidance from people he knows
frustrations: Portals that his staff have to fight with
personas.tone: Warm, experienced, a bit traditional, values loyalty
personas.voice_sample: I don't live in my inbox. Sit down with me, show me the data, and tell me which of my patients this is for.
what_earns_engagement: A well-prepared rep with modular, MLR-approved leave-behinds
A peer speaker program with a cardiologist he respects
A light email recap that reinforces — never replaces — the visit

personas.name: Dr. Priya Nair
personas.tagline: The coordinated omnichannel prescriber who wants a mix, not a channel
personas.bio: Busy rheumatologist who rarely sees reps in person anymore but actively opens email, attends webinars and joins virtual details. She wants a joined-up experience — she notices, and dislikes, when the same message chases her across five channels.

prescribing.brand_stance: pragmatic switcher when the journey is coherent and access is smooth

tolerated: Selective in-person for a genuinely new topic
channels.f2f_stance: Open to occasional in-person, but virtual-first
channels.email_stance: Engages when timing and relevance are right; hates message whiplash
channels.best_moment: Lunchtime webinars, evening catch-up on email

personas.tone: Measured, organized, quietly demanding of quality
personas.voice_sample: Give me one clear story across email, webinar and a virtual detail — sequenced, not shouted five times.
what_earns_engagement: A sequenced trigger → reinforce → convert journey with one message architecture
A strong lunchtime webinar
Signals-based next-best-channel instead of blasting every channel

personas.name: Prof. David Whitmore
personas.setting: Academic medical center / NCI-designated cancer center
personas.tagline: The guideline-shaping thought leader who is allergic to promotion
personas.bio: Publishes, sits on guideline committees and speaks at ASH/ASCO. He engages with the full primary dataset and mechanism, through medical affairs — not commercial. Promotional messaging in a scientific context is an instant turn-off and a compliance red flag to him.

prescribing.brand_stance: evidence-led; influences hundreds of downstream prescribers

digital.rep_access: medical affairs only — no commercial reps

tolerated: Peer-reviewed data emails from medical, clearly non-promotional
avoided: Branded promotional messaging in scientific channels
channels.f2f_stance: Engages in person at congresses and advisory boards
channels.email_stance: Reads data-driven medical communications; ignores promo

frustrations: Being treated as a volume target
decision_drivers: Depth of primary data and mechanism
personas.tone: Erudite, rigorous, sceptical of anything that smells commercial
personas.voice_sample: If your plan pushes branded claims at me through a scientific channel, we're done. Bring me the primary data through medical affairs.
what_earns_engagement: A medical-affairs-led scientific exchange with the full evidence base
A congress or advisory-board touchpoint
Strict separation of promotional and scientific content

personas.name: Dr. Sofia Alvarez
personas.tagline: The time-poor generalist who needs the answer in ten seconds, in workflow
personas.bio: Sees 25+ patients a day. She will use something the moment it's fast, clear and lives where she already works — the EHR and her phone. Anything that adds a step or a login loses her before lunch.

prescribing.brand_stance: will start the right patient if selection is obvious and access is frictionless

tolerated: A 5-minute virtual detail if it saves her time later
channels.f2f_stance: Occasional brief in-person; time is the constraint
channels.email_stance: Opens short, scannable email; abandons anything dense

motivations: Ready-to-use patient materials and access shortcuts
frustrations: Anything that slows her clinic down
personas.tone: Warm but rushed, practical, no patience for fluff
personas.voice_sample: I have ninety seconds. Tell me which patient, what dose, and how they afford it — inside my EHR, ideally.
what_earns_engagement: A point-of-care / EHR nudge with clear patient selection
A short email with a copay card and a one-page patient handout
Zero added workflow steps

personas.name: Dr. Robert Feld
personas.tagline: The conservative prescriber who needs durable outcomes and peer proof before he moves
personas.bio: Cautious by temperament and training. He waits for long-term outcomes, real-world evidence and guideline endorsement, and watches what respected peers do before changing practice. Novelty-led messaging makes him more skeptical, not less.

prescribing.brand_stance: skeptical; low baseline engagement; converts slowly over many credible touches

tolerated: A data-dense email if it's outcomes, not hype
channels.f2f_stance: Values in-person evidence discussion with a knowledgeable rep or peer
channels.email_stance: Reads only if it leads with hard outcomes and guidelines

personas.tone: Reserved, exacting, quietly resistant to marketing
personas.voice_sample: Show me the five-year outcomes and where it sits in the guidelines. I'm not switching my patients for a launch splash.
what_earns_engagement: Evidence-first content leading with durability, safety and guideline status
Peer proof and real-world evidence
A patient, multi-touch nurture — not a hard push

personas.name: Dr. Hannah Kim
personas.setting: Private dermatology group with an active social presence
personas.tagline: The digitally fluent younger derm who lives on mobile and peer communities
personas.bio: Younger, digitally fluent dermatologist active in online peer communities and comfortable with virtual everything. She researches on mobile between patients and trusts curated peer discussion as much as a rep.

prescribing.brand_stance: willing to try new mechanisms early if the digital experience and access are good

channels.f2f_stance: Rarely in person; prefers virtual and asynchronous
channels.email_stance: High engagement with relevant, well-designed mobile email
channels.best_moment: Between patients on mobile; evenings in peer forums

decision_drivers: Speed to clear skin / results data
personas.voice_sample: If it's not on my phone and my peers aren't talking about it, it doesn't exist. Make it mobile and make it credible.
what_earns_engagement: Presence in trusted peer digital communities
Mobile-first email and short video
A frictionless digital patient-support/copay experience

personas.name: Grace Okafor
personas.condition: Newly diagnosed HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer
personas.tagline: The newly diagnosed patient who is frightened and drowning in information
personas.bio: Diagnosed six weeks ago. She's scared, googling everything at midnight, and struggling to separate credible information from noise. She wants plain language, reassurance and to know what happens next — not branded claims or scary statistics.

tolerated: Gentle branded education once she's oriented
channels.f2f_stance: Trusts her care team most; wants human reassurance
channels.email_stance: Opens supportive, plain-language email; overwhelmed by dense content

personas.voice_sample: Please just tell me what this means and what happens next — in words I understand. Don't sell to me right now.
what_earns_engagement: Unbranded, empathetic, plain-language education
A clear 'what happens next' and questions-to-ask tool
A gentle path to patient support — not a branded pitch

personas.name: Tom Reyes
personas.tagline: The informed, self-advocating patient who researches as hard as his doctor
personas.bio: Diagnosed years ago and deeply engaged in his own care. He's in online communities, tracks his symptoms in an app, reads trial data and expects transparency on cost and access. He can tell when content is thin, and hates being talked down to.

tolerated: Detailed clinical content — the more the better
avoided: Being oversimplified or talked down to
channels.f2f_stance: Comes to appointments prepared with his own research
channels.email_stance: Engages deeply with rich, transparent email

motivations: Detailed treatment info and shared decision-making
personas.tone: Confident, informed, expects to be treated as a partner
personas.voice_sample: I've read the trial. Don't hand me a pamphlet — give me the real data, the real cost, and a say in my own treatment.
what_earns_engagement: Depth, self-service tools and shared-decision resources
Full transparency on cost and access
Respecting him as an expert in his own disease

personas.name: Linda Park
personas.condition: Care partner for husband with advanced prostate cancer
personas.tagline: The care partner who manages the regimen and is usually overlooked
personas.bio: Manages her husband's appointments, medications, side effects and logistics. She's the one who actually administers and tracks therapy, yet most campaigns talk past her. She needs practical, clear support and to be acknowledged as a decision influencer.

channels.f2f_stance: Values nurse educators and human support lines
channels.best_moment: Early morning and late evening around care duties

decision_drivers: Practical support that reduces her burden
personas.voice_sample: I'm the one giving the injections and tracking the side effects. Talk to me too — and make it simpler to manage.
what_earns_engagement: Content that addresses the caregiver explicitly
Simplified regimen logistics and adherence tools
Access to nurse educators and support services

personas.name: Walter Nguyen
personas.tagline: The disengaged patient who quietly stops taking it when it gets hard or costly
personas.bio: On several medications and quietly non-adherent. Cost surprises, complex regimens and guilt-tinged messaging push him further away. Simple reminders, affordability help and small encouragements are what actually keep him on therapy.

channels.f2f_stance: Trusts his pharmacist; limited other contact
channels.email_stance: Rarely opens email; SMS is the reliable channel

personas.voice_sample: When it costs too much or gets complicated, I just stop. Make it simple and don't make me feel bad about it.
what_earns_engagement: Low-friction SMS reminders and refill/copay help
Positive reinforcement, never guilt
Removing cost and complexity barriers
